heading: No fixed list of platform actions
body:
Tachyon does not put a list of verbs (fixed platform actions) between an application and its platform. A notification and a file dialog belong to the platform. A service written in the platform's own language can already use them. A fixed list in the middle could contain only the part that Tachyon had built. That part would have to exist in three hosts, for every platform at once. An application would be limited to that part.

So in the browser, a JavaScript or TypeScript service uses web APIs. A service in another language uses Tachyon's small set of browser APIs (`Clock`, `SecureRandom`, `Connectivity`, `PageVisibility`, `Preferences`, `Clipboard`, `Share`, `Notifications` and `Geolocation`), or gets other browser values from a JavaScript or TypeScript service through an event. Python services do not have Tachyon's browser APIs yet (see "What each service language can use in the browser"). A service that is linked into a native app has no page, so the build refuses these browser APIs in it (`TY1317`). The native side uses AppKit, UIKit, the Android framework or Win32, each from the language that already works with it. A tray icon is declared in the manifest instead (`tac.application.tray`, ADR 0107), because it needs the host to hide and show the window.
